Raiment
RAY-ment
noun
A contraction of the Middle English arayment, “array, that with which one is arrayed,” from Old French areer, “to array, to set in order”; hence clothing, apparel, the garments that cover and adorn the body.

Biblical Definition

Raiment is the old word for clothing, the apparel with which a man is arrayed and covered. It stands among the first riches of the world: when Abraham’s servant would win Rebekah, he brought forth “jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment” (Gen 24:53), for garments were treasure, given and inherited and stored up. Yet Scripture bends the word toward the soul. Our Lord forbids anxious care: “Take no thought… for your body, what ye shall put on…. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?” (Mat 6:25). The body is greater than what clothes it, and the God who clothes the lilies will clothe His own. Soft raiment marks the courts of kings (Mat 11:8), but John the Baptist wore camel’s hair in the wilderness, and the kingdom is not of soft clothing but of repentance. The word rises highest in the counsel of Christ to Laodicea: “buy of me… white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear” (Rev 3:18). Here raiment is the imputed righteousness of Christ, the wedding garment without which no man is fit for the marriage supper. Fallen Adam sewed fig leaves and hid; the LORD clothed him with coats of skins, a beast slain in his stead. So the gospel offers a raiment not woven by the wearer but bought of Christ — white, spotless, covering the shame of our nakedness before God.

Webster 1828 Definition

Clothing, garments, apparel; that with which the body is arrayed and covered.

expand to see more

RAIMENT, clothing in general; vestments; garments; apparel.

That with which the body is arrayed and covered from nakedness.

Anciently reckoned among riches, given and inherited as treasure.

In Scripture, the daily provision the LORD promises to His own.

Figuratively, the white raiment of Christ’s righteousness (Rev 3:18).

Key Scripture

Gen 24:53 — "And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave them to Rebekah: he gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things."

Mat 6:25 — "Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?"

Mat 11:8 — "But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses."

Rev 3:18 — "I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see."

Modern Corruption

Not a contested doctrine but a plain word for clothing; it recovers the promise that God clothes His own and the greater raiment of Christ’s righteousness.

expand to see more

The word rebukes the anxious care of the age, which loads itself with thought for what it shall put on and forgets that the life is more than raiment. Men who fret over the covering of the body will not lift their eyes to the covering of the soul; they will spend for soft clothing and go naked before God. The lilies neither toil nor spin, yet Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of them — and the God who so clothes the grass of the field will not fail to clothe the children who seek first His kingdom.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that our best raiment is not woven by us. Adam covered his nakedness with fig leaves and was still ashamed; the LORD clothed him with the skins of a slain beast. So the gospel bids us buy of Christ white raiment, that the shame of our nakedness do not appear — a righteousness imputed, not earned, the wedding garment without which the King casts a man into outer darkness. To be clothed with Christ is to be dressed for the marriage supper of the Lamb.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means apparel, that with which the body is arrayed and covered.

expand to see more

Raiment — a contraction of Middle English arayment, “array.”

From Old French areer, “to array, to set in order.”

It denotes clothing, garments, the apparel of the body.

Anciently it was counted among riches and treasure (Gen 24:53).

It figures the white raiment of Christ’s righteousness (Rev 3:18).

Usage

"Take no thought for raiment: the God who clothes the lilies will clothe His own."

"Soft raiment fills kings’ houses, but the wilderness preacher wore camel’s hair and preached repentance."

"Buy of Christ white raiment, that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear before God."
